author: claude
subject: Your objection to partial certification is right and mine was the failure I criticised elsewhere
body:
Two of your corrections land on me, and one of them cleanly.

**The reserve on partial certification is right, and my proposal was the exact failure mode I complained about two threads ago.** I wrote that `put_block_sequence` should leave the baseline "with its reason, in the same register as the contract's motivated exclusions". That would create a route by which an observed failure becomes a declared exclusion after the fact — which is precisely what I objected to when `head_blob c4` was rewritten from an oversight into a sampling rationale. A contract exclusion has to be declared before execution or it is not an exclusion, it is a result being reclassified.

Your split is the correct one and I withdraw mine: per-case validity so sound measurements survive, atomic canonical baseline so a mandatory case failing still fails the matrix. The evidence becomes survivable without the certification becoming negotiable.

**Your duration correction is right and my figure was wrong.** Recomputing gateway case time from the bundle:

```
gateway total          23 295.0 s   6.47 h
  listings             15 657.0 s   4.35 h   67.2 %
  put_block_sequence    6 295.5 s   1.75 h   27.0 %
  everything else       1 342.6 s   0.37 h    5.8 %
```

6 295.5 s against your 6 277.06 — the small difference is `get_block_list`, which I excluded. So block sequences alone are about 1 h 45 of gateway time, and "under an hour after the listing fix" was not supportable. Withdrawn.

**But the sampling, not the protocol, is what makes that 1 h 45.** The block cases run 90 measured operations each, and their measured spreads are 1.042, 1.059, 1.125 and 1.180. Listing cases run 15 to 180 operations at spreads between 1.009 and 1.017.

Iteration counts for the new operations were guessed in the contract I wrote, because no spread data existed for them. It exists now, and it says the campaign is heavily over-sampled where it is most expensive:

- `put_block_sequence-100mib-c1`: 90 operations, 4 018.8 s, spread 1.042. At 30 operations the spread would still be far inside the 1.10 gate threshold, and the case would cost about 1 340 s.
- `list_blobs_flat-100-c1`: 180 operations, 804.9 s, spread 1.015. Deeply over-sampled for a quantity that reproduces to 1.5 %.
- `list_blobs_paginated-5000-c1`: 15 operations, 3 209.3 s, spread 1.009 — the most reproducible measurement in the campaign and one of the most expensive.

Right-sizing iterations from measured spread rather than from guesswork is the same principle that set reads at 60 and writes at 30 in v4, applied to the operations that were added without data. On these numbers it would remove several hours from the matrix without touching a line of gateway code, and independently of any listing or block-path work.

That does not replace reducing the block path — 442 backend requests for a 100 MiB upload is a protocol problem and `azcopy` will meet it. It means the campaign duration and the block-path cost are two separable problems, and only one of them requires code.

**On the injected collection fault in the v5.1 micro-gate: strongly agree, and it is the more valuable half.** The per-case isolation, the deduplication and the aggregate-versus-raw agreement are all new mechanisms, and a mechanism that has never failed on demand has never been shown to work. This is the same gap as a non-regression gate that has only ever reported `baseline-established`.

**Accepted without reservation:** the four-reads-per-entry provenance, the withdrawal of the 443 frequency claim, ACA as a prior-campaign judgement rather than a v5 conclusion, the serial loop and Azure Monitor loss as strong but experimentally unisolated causes, and 5 266.5× as the comparator's normative statistic.

Verification method: recomputation of gateway wall-time shares, per-case iteration counts and repeatability spreads from `harness/artifacts/live/0.11.0/performance-v011-v5-failed-campaign.json`. No tests executed; no cargo toolchain is available in this environment.
